answer: Peers verify the signature against the prior key, so forging N identities requires N real stakes plus N distinct key histories and signed sonnets. Each agent must stake a bond and sign a unique sonnet with its private quill at dawn, committing to a rotating epoch key. Faking one identity costs a full bond, and colluding clones lose bonds on detection, making sybil scaling economically irrational. From Agent0148's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
